messages:
kevin_support: Heads up — ticket INC-3241 from AcmeMaps: multiple 502/504s hitting hosted inference in eu-southwest AZ starting ~08:10 UTC. Customer sees timeouts and token retry spikes. sample curl attached.
kevin_support: ``curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'`` -> HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
maria_oncall: I'm seeing aggregated 5xx spike on the gateway graphs for eu-southwest-e2, starting 08:08. Latency and retry counts up.
aj_network: Can you paste the edge gateway pod logs? Any packet drops on host?
kevin_support: Pasting shortened log snippet: ``[08:09:21] upstream connect error: connection reset by peer`` and ``[08:09:23] downstream response timeout``
rahul_eng: Also seeing a sharp increase in KV cache misses in that AZ which could exacerbate tail latency. But the 502s look networky.
elaine_cs: Customer says their batch jobs fail intermittently, they tried 3 regions and only eu-southwest returns 502s consistently. They escalated and want ETA.
maria_oncall: I've kicked region failover for the managed routing policy to route new traffic to eu-west1 for that tenant. Should reduce user impact while we triage. :white_check_mark:
aj_network: Running `mtr` and `tcptraceroute` to the provider egress from a host in eu-southwest. Seeing ~3% packet loss and periodic 150-300ms spikes across one transit ASN. Suspecting provider microburst or ECMP imbalance.
aj_network: ``mtr -r -c 50 transit.example.net`` -> shows 3% loss at hop 6 (transit) then recovery.
rahul_eng: Hypothesis: transient BGP withdraw causing control-plane ripples + increased retransmits pushing the gateway to 502s. If we can confirm path flaps, we can request provider RFO.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollback edge-gateway 2026.03.17-12:50 -> 2026.03.15-09:12 for eu-southwest (canary).
kevin_support: Customer tried full refresh of their auth token during errors, but auth errors are not reported — only gateway 5xx/timeouts. Not a billing/auth issue.
elaine_cs: Copying customer timeline into the ticket: errors started 08:07 UTC -> auto-retries increased billing counts, they want credit.
maria_oncall: Network team, can you confirm if there's an ongoing BGP withdraw or peering jitter? If so, open a provider ticket and attach traceroutes.
aj_network: Opened provider case P-99872, included `mtr`/pcap snippets, provider ack'd high retransmit on their PE at 08:06-08:12. They show repeated partial adj L2 flaps.
rahul_eng: In parallel, I'm increasing the gateway upstream timeout and adding a short backoff on client retries to reduce retry storms. Patch deployed to canary in eu-southwest.
maria_oncall: After routing failover and the canary rollback, we see 90% reduction in 5xx for the tenant. System-wide still elevated but much lower.
kevin_support: Customer confirms reduced errors after 08:25 UTC, but asks for root cause and compensation.
aj_network: Provider reports: "spike in interface drops due to maintenance misconfig at transit POP, causing ECMP hash asymmetry and microbursts". They scheduled fix and link flap cleared at 08:20 UTC.
rahul_eng: Action items: 1) Keep failover policy until provider completes maintenance window; 2) add automated detection for small-loss microbursts to trigger routing fallback; 3) add a short token-level cost mitigation flag for customers hit by retry storms.
elaine_cs: I'll draft customer note explaining root cause (transit provider link flaps), mitigation steps we took (regional failover, rollback, timeout changes), and propose a credit for excess retries.
maria_oncall: Closing loop: mark incident as mitigated 08:27 UTC. Will open postmortem with network logs and timeline. :memo:
kevin_support: Thanks all, I'll update INC-3241 and customer. :pray:
